title: Optimizing Wigner Negativity in Scattering Processes Using Energetic Cost Functions
authors: Kian Hwee Lim, Kiarn T. Laverick, Sahil Sardar Jafar, Samyak P. Prasad, Maria Maffei, Alexia Auffèves
abstract: Wigner negativities (WNs) are key signatures of non-Gaussian bosonic states and essential resources for quantum technologies. We study their generation in the scattering of coherent pulses by a two-level atom coupled to a one-dimensional reservoir, a unitary and energy-preserving platform. Optimization in this multimode setting is hindered by the complexity of evaluating Wigner functions. We overcome this challenge by introducing energetic cost functions that identify output modes most likely to host large negativities. First using incoherent energy and then isolating a genuinely non-Gaussian contribution, we demonstrate a strong correlation between these quantities and WNs. This correlation extends beyond short, intense pulses to encompass pulses of finite energy, where photons are scattered while the two-level atom is driven. Focusing on the energy-efficiency of the process, we show that maximally efficient generation takes place for one input photon, on average, spectrally mode-matched with the atom.
summary: This paper develops a method using energetic cost functions to optimize the generation of Wigner Negativity, a key signature of non-Gaussian bosonic states. The study models coherent pulse scattering from a two-level atom coupled to a reservoir. It finds that maximal efficiency for generating these non-classical resources occurs under specific conditions involving single-photon input and spectral matching.
main_problem: The research aims to optimize the generation of Wigner Negativity (WN) signatures, which characterize non-Gaussian bosonic states, during quantum scattering processes.
main_result: Maximally efficient WN generation is achieved when the input pulse contains an average of one photon and is spectrally mode-matched with the two-level atom (TLA).
method: The authors introduce energetic cost functions to bypass direct, complex evaluation of Wigner functions in multimode scattering settings.
model_or_system: The system models a coherent pulse scattering off a Two-Level Atom (TLA) coupled to a one-dimensional bosonic reservoir. The dynamics are governed by an energy-preserving Hamiltonian and analyzed using quantum optical kernels.
key_observables: Wigner Negativity ($\mathcal{N}_W$), Incoherent Energy ($E_{	ext{inc}}$), Squeezing Energy ($E_S$), Mixedness Energy ($E_M$), and Non-Gaussian Energy ($E_{NG}$).
important_parameters: The optimal regime is found near the condition of one average input photon ($\langle\alphaangle^2=1$) and spectral mode matching.
main_assumptions: Approximations include using energetic cost functions to correlate with WN, and employing finite rank approximations for kernel calculations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the correlation between various energy components ($E_{	ext{inc}}$ vs $\mathcal{N}_{	ext{inc}}$, $E_{NG}$ vs $\mathcal{N}_{ng}$) across different input pulse parameters $(\alpha, \Delta)$, identifying the optimal operating point.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical model and Hamiltonian, develops the energetic cost function approach to circumvent Wigner function complexity, analyzes the correlation between energy components and WN, and concludes by pinpointing the optimal operational regime for high-efficiency generation.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful theoretical tool—energetic cost functions—to quantify non-Gaussian resources like Wigner Negativity in complex open quantum systems (TLA coupled to reservoirs), which is highly relevant for quantum light sources and quantum information processing.
